titles.469: Annotatio III §.X (5): Natura Sacramentorum — at least a triple assault on sacrament-nature
titles.470: Annotatio III §.X (5)(1)–(2): Removes the material Sign; turns Signatum into the Sacrament of Signatum itself
titles.471: Annotatio III §.X (5)(3): Eliminates the sacramental proposition — bread gone when the priest says Hoc est Corpus meum
titles.472: Annotatio III §.X (6): Ratio / Philosophy theoretical — overturns substance, accident, spirit, body, place, penetration
titles.473: Annotatio III §.X (6) cont.: Admits sign-accidents that must enter the substances; practical enmity — oral God-eating (Cicero / Averroes)
titles.474: Annotatio III §.X (6) close: Natural humanity — corporal chewing of Christ’s flesh vs Lev. blood ban; stop before §.XI (7) Sense

latin.469: (5.) Natura Sacramentorum, nomine ad minimum triplici.
latin.470: (1.) Quòd Signum Materiale, alteram sacramenti partem essentialem, ex Eucharistia submovet, panem nempe & vinum, solis remanentibus harum substantiarum accidentibus, ut substantialitate omni, ex sententia Pontificiorum, ita & Materialitate, casssis. (2) Quòd Signatum Sacramenti Eucharistici (Corpus nempe & Sanguinem Christi) in ipsum Signati Sacramentum Corporis & Sanguinis Christi, commutat.
latin.471: (3) Quòd propositionem sacramentalem ipsâ hujus pronuntiatione, sacramento Eucharistiæ eliminat, pane non amplius superstite, dum de pane sacerdos propositionem hanc finit: Hoc, seu hic panis est Corpus meum.
latin.472: (6.) Rationi Emaculatiori, i. e. Philosophiæ, tùm Theoreticæ, tum Practicæ. Priori quidem, dum primarum ac præcipuarum rerum, Substantiæ puta & Accidentis, Spiritus & Corporis, Penetrabilitatis & Impenetrabilitatis, Extensionis & Localitatis essentiales Ideas ac Definitiones invertit ac concutit, Substantiam Finitam definitamque accidentibus suis essentialibus exuendo, Accidentia ab Inhæsione, in substantia, actuali absolvendo, corpus & sanguinem Christi in spiritum commutando, per negatam iisdem tum extensionem, tùm impenetrationem tùm localitatem, humanis corporibus essentialiter debitas, indeque nec per miracula, ab essentiarum ad unum omnium finitarum Autore, etsi pro Lubitu suô Annihilatore quoque potentissimo, contradictoria interim nulla, idque per & propter omnipotentiam suam, admissuro, destituendas.
latin.473: Prætereà Species & Accidentia Signorum, panis & vini, admittendo tales, quæ tamen signorum horum substantias necessariò ingrediuntur, e.g. Panis quantitatem ab Extensione ejus definita, ipsôque, adeo pane, realiter haud diversam; Vini Motum in Calice, Accidentibus nudis i. e. omni substantialitate orbis, minimè competentem, visum verò in subtilioribus vini, calice comprehensi, particulis, exhalaturis cum tempore, vinique massam substantialem, evolutione suâ imminuturis. Practica verò Philosophiæ inimica imminet Transsubstantiatio, quando etiam pietatem, in Deum, naturalem, & naturalem humanitatem arietat. PIETATEM IN DEUM, afferendo, Deum oraliter manducari: Ecquemnam tam amentem esse putas, qui id, quô vescitur, Deum esse credat? quærit Cicero de Natura Deorum Lib. 3. Cui respondet Averrois judicium sententiaque de Christianismo: Omnes regiones peragravi, nec Christianâ gente deteriorem ullam reperi: Quia quem Deum adorant, hunc dentibus devorant. vid. Dionys. Carthus. in 4. Dist. 10. Art. 1. Confer B. Hotting. Eucharist. defens. pag. 214. & seqq.
latin.474: Dein HUMANITATEM QUOQUE NATURALEM Communemque, statuendo jubendoque Carnem Christi humanam, corporali ore manducandam & sanguinem ejus humanum, ore corporali hauriendum bibendumque, Actiones hoc pacto imperando, à quibus humana Natura, nondum in brutam degenerata, sponte suâ abhorret & ut abhorreret tantò certiùs, olim, in gente Judaica, ab omni animantium sanguine abstinendum esse, disertô à DEO præcepto cautum fuisse legitur, Lev. 7. vers. 27. & cap. 17. 14.

pass_a.469: (5.) By the Nature of the Sacraments, under at least a triple name.
pass_a.470: (1.) That it removes from the Eucharist the Material Sign, the other essential part of a sacrament — namely bread and wine — only the accidents of these substances remaining, void as of all substantiality, in the Pontificians’ sentence, so also of Materiality. (2) That it changes the Signatum of the Eucharistic Sacrament (namely Christ’s Body and Blood) into the very Sacrament of the Signatum of Christ’s Body and Blood.
pass_a.471: (3) That by the very pronunciation of this it eliminates the sacramental proposition from the Sacrament of the Eucharist, bread no longer surviving, while concerning bread the priest finishes this proposition: This, or this bread, is My Body.
pass_a.472: (6.) To cleaner Reason, i.e. to Philosophy, both Theoretical and Practical. To the former indeed, while it inverts and shakes the essential Ideas and Definitions of the first and chief things — Substance and Accident, Spirit and Body, Penetrability and Impenetrability, Extension and Locality — by stripping a Finite and defined Substance of its essential accidents, absolving Accidents from actual Inherence in a substance, changing Christ’s body and blood into spirit by denying them extension, impenetration and locality essentially owed to human bodies, and so to be destituted not even by miracles by the Author of all finite essences unto one, although as most powerful Annihilator also at His pleasure, yet admitting no contradictories meanwhile, and that through and because of His omnipotence.
pass_a.473: Besides by admitting Species and Accidents of the Signs, bread and wine, of such a kind as nonetheless necessarily enter these signs’ substances — e.g. the bread’s quantity, from its defined Extension, and so not really diverse from the bread itself; the wine’s Motion in the Cup, least competent to bare Accidents i.e. emptied of all substantiality, yet seen in the subtler particles of wine held in the cup, which will exhale with time and by their flight diminish the wine’s substantial mass. But Transsubstantiation also threatens as enemy of Practical Philosophy when it also butts natural piety toward God and natural humanity. PIETY TOWARD GOD, by asserting God is eaten orally: Whom do you think so mad as to believe that what he feeds on is God? asks Cicero, De Natura Deorum bk. 3. To which answers Averroes’s judgment and sentence on Christianity: I have traversed all regions, and found no race worse than the Christian: Because the God they adore, they devour with their teeth. See Dionysius the Carthusian on 4 Dist. 10 Art. 1; compare Blessed Hottinger, Defense of the Eucharist pp. 214ff.
pass_a.474: Then NATURAL and common HUMANITY also, by stating and commanding Christ’s human Flesh to be eaten with the corporal mouth and His human blood to be drawn and drunk with the corporal mouth — by this pact commanding Actions from which human Nature, not yet degenerated into the brute, spontaneously abhors; and that it might abhor the more certainly, once among the Jewish people it is read to have been expressly guarded by GOD’s precept that one must abstain from all blood of living things, Lev. 7:27 and ch. 17:14.

469: (5) Transsubstantiation assaults the Nature of the Sacraments under at least three heads.
Strimesius marks the assault as at minimum triple — three named wounds to what a sacrament is.
470: (1) It removes the material Sign — bread and wine — leaving only accidents, void of substantiality and (on their view) of materiality too.
(2) It turns the Signatum (Christ’s body and blood) into the sacrament of that Signatum itself — sign and thing collapse.
471: (3) By the priest’s pronunciation it kills the sacramental proposition.
Bread no longer survives while he finishes of bread: ‘This, or this bread, is My Body.’
472: It overturns essential ideas of substance and accident, spirit and body, penetrability, extension, locality: strips finite substance of essential accidents, frees accidents from inherence, spirits Christ’s body by denying extension, impenetrability, and place — which even omnipotence will not admit as contradictories via miracle.
473: It also admits bread/wine species that must enter those substances (bread’s quantity not really other than the bread; wine’s motion in the cup unfit for bare accidents, yet seen in exhalable particles that shrink the wine-mass).

Practical philosophy too: it butts natural piety — oral God-eating. Cicero: who is mad enough to think what he eats is God? Averroes: no worse race than Christians, who devour with teeth the God they adore (Hottinger pp. 214ff).
474: It also butts natural common humanity: commanding Christ’s human flesh chewed and His blood drunk with the corporal mouth — acts unfallen human nature spontaneously abhors.
God once expressly barred the Jewish people from all animal blood (Lev. 7:27; 17:14) so that abhorrence would be the surer.
